status: PARTIAL -- token usage measured for codex; dollar cost NOT comparable across CLIs

what_was_measured.task: create hello.txt containing exactly 'hi' (identical to the latency comparison)

codex.note: codex prints a token total; on the ChatGPT free tier the user pays $0 regardless of tokens

opencode.note: opencode printed NO token or cost line for this run, so nothing was measured. Not recorded as zero.

why_no_dollar_comparison: A dollar figure needs per-model token pricing AND a measured token count from each tool. opencode reported no tokens, so any cost number for it would be invented. Publishing 'codex $X vs opencode $Y' with Y fabricated would be exactly the false-green this project exists to prevent.
what_our_engine_does_capture: autonomy/run.sh _read_iteration_cost reads .loki/metrics/result-cost-<iter>.json for input_tokens, output_tokens and total_cost_usd, and efficiency_cost.collect_efficiency folds them while keeping 'not recorded' (usd=None) distinct from a genuine $0.00. That is authoritative for the Claude path; free-tier CLIs do not emit that file.
not_claimed: No cost ranking between tools. No claim that a cheap model is cheaper for equivalent quality: that needs the same spec run to completion on both a cheap and a flagship model with cost recorded on both sides, which requires paid API access this session did not use.
what_would_close_it: Run one identical multi-iteration spec end to end on (a) a flagship via API with cost recording and (b) a cheap model, then compare recorded cost per completed spec. De-risk ONE cell first; a bench cell that times out before its writer runs produces no result file and a matrix runner that greps stdout advances silently.
